newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty holds below resistance, depos ease.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty holds below resistance, depos ease.

text.p: The Polish zloty on Tuesday walked a tightrope just under strong resistance at 2.5 percent from the parity rate and succeeded in not setting off a central bank intervention, dealers said.
They said foreign investor payments for T-bills bought at Monday's primary auction kept the zloty pinned to resistance.
"The zloty was around 2.5 percent all day with any gains likely to spark an intervention," said one foreign bank dealer.
The zloty closed at 2.55/2.49 percent from the trading band centre against Monday's 2.52/2.47 percent close.
It closed at 3.1460/75 to the dollar, down from 3.1400/20 on Monday and at 1.8515/30 to the mark, up from 1.8552/57.

The central bank said the current account gap in the first quarter grew to $1.49 billion from a $151 million surplus in the first three months of 1996. Official currency reserves eased slightly to $17.98 billion in the first quarter.
Dealers said the data had no immididiate imact on markets, but rather reinforced views that the C/A gap and large imports were inflated by fast growing domestic demand.

"It is not surprising that Poland has such a C/A deficit as its economy is growing at around seven percent, while demand for investment is more than (year-on-year) 20 percent," said Krzysztof Bledowski, chief economist at WoodCommerz in Warsaw.

On the money market one-day rates slipped after the central bank did not stage an open market operation on Tuesday after nearly one billion zlotys worth of bids was rejected at Monday's T-bill auction.
Overnight and tomorrow/next rates both fell about 0.1 point from opening to 22.35/22.55 and 22.55/22.70 percent.
